child_tree_fix.adoption: After leader wait, enumerate only /proc/<controller>/task/<controller>/children. Every adopted child uses pidfd, nonreaping wait and independent waitpid/close. If pidfd allocation fails, preserve that error and use only the kernel-proven unreaped own-child relationship for bounded cleanup.
child_tree_fix.close_scope: Leader pidfd, every adopted pidfd and both output files close independently; FD/child failures prevent aggregate success.
child_tree_fix.command_identity: Existing start_new_session=True. Leader exit observed through pidfd waitid WNOWAIT; this reserves its original PID before same-session/PGID validation and group SIGKILL. No group signal after leader reaping.
child_tree_fix.controller_only_subreaper: PR_GET/SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER on this PID only; original flag retained and restored after exact kernel ECHILD. Single-threaded and default SIGCHLD required, no preexisting children allowed.
child_tree_fix.empty_gate: Before every next command and final restoration, fixed own child list is empty and waitid(P_ALL, WNOWAIT) must report ECHILD.
child_tree_fix.failure_policy: Original start/wait/exit error is first; cleanup/capture/close errors append. Orphaned descendants cause build-command failure even when cleanup succeeds. No retry/reconnect/new build attempt.
child_tree_fix.limits: At most 128 adopted children and one shared 5-second cleanup deadline per command. Unexpected direct cleanup uses the same deadline. Actual elapsed recorded without capping.
child_tree_fix.origin: Root independent review of exact build01 and C16 resource guard; fixed gcc/clang link drivers may fork helpers. Resource guard only samples its own cgroup; it does not reap descendants.
child_tree_fix.process_scope: Only this controller's command process trees. No global /proc scan or claim about unrelated ancestors/wrappers; durable outer terminal still required.

controls.C_scope: Pure explicit backend seams; no Android property syscall, UID change or child creation in C controls.
